source_text: Si autem dixeris utrumque iustum esse, et quod nos dicimus et quod vos, id est et quod lex Dei sanxit et quod Manichaeus Traducianusque confinxit, hic sane rationis perspicuae potentiam cohibentes benignius te convenimus et mitius. Cur ergo, si creditis et hoc bonum esse quod dicimus, et illud bonum esse quod dicitis, tantis totam Italiam factionibus commovistis? Cur seditiones Romae conductis populis excitastis? Cur de sumptibus pauperum saginastis per totam pene Africam equorum greges, quos prosequente Alypio tribunis et centurionibus destinastis? Cur matronarum oblatis haereditatibus potestates saeculi corrupistis, ut in nos stipula publici furoris arderet? Cur dissipastis ecclesiarum quietem? Cur religiosi principis tempora persecutionum impietate maculastis, si a nobis nihil aliud dicitur, quam quod etiam tu bonum cogeris confiteri?
pass_a_gloss: But if you have said that both are just, both what we say and what you say, that is both what the law of God sanctioned and what the Manichaean and the advocate of inherited sin have invented, here indeed restraining the power of clear reason we convene you more kindly and more mildly. Why therefore, if you believe both this which we say is good and that which you say is good, have you moved all Italy with such factions? Why have you stirred seditions at Rome with hired peoples? Why from the expenses of the poor have you fattened throughout almost all Africa herds of horses, which with Alypius accompanying you destined to tribunes and centurions? Why by offered inheritances of matrons have you corrupted the powers of the age, that the stubble of public fury might burn against us? Why have you scattered the quiet of the churches? Why have you stained the times of a religious prince with the impiety of persecutions, if nothing other is said by us than what even you are forced to confess is good?

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: But if you say both are just, both what we say and what you say—that is, both what God’s law decreed and what Mani and the advocate of inherited sin invented—then, restraining the force of plain reason, we question you more gently and kindly. If you believe both what we say and what you say to be good, why have you stirred up all Italy with so much organized intrigue? Why have you hired crowds to raise riots in Rome? Why have you fed herds of horses throughout almost all Africa at the poor’s expense and sent them, with Alypius escorting them, to tribunes and centurions? Why have you corrupted worldly officials with the estates offered by wealthy women, so that the tinder of public fury would blaze against us? Why have you shattered the churches’ peace? Why have you stained a religious emperor’s reign with the wickedness of persecution, if we say nothing except what even you are forced to acknowledge as good?

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.
